title: Named volumes versus bind mounts: which to use when

videos.script: Lesson seven lost a table. This lesson keeps it, in three different ways. {{volume}} A named volume first. Docker creates it and looks after it, and it outlives every container. Ana removes the database container, starts a new one, and the row is still there. {{bind}} Then a bind mount: a folder of the host, shown inside the container. Ana edits a file on the host, and the container sees the change at once. Then a file written by the container turns out to belong to root, and one flag fixes it. {{tmpfs}} And a tmpfs, which lives in memory and is gone when the container stops. {{choose}} One question decides between them: who owns the files? The application, a person, or nobody.
